profile.reading:
Csquare IAD4-B sits at 21571 Beaumeade Circle, Ashburn, Virginia 20147, one of two street addresses (21561 and 21571 Beaumeade Circle) Csquare's own spec sheet lists under its single "IAD4" campus heading. Csquare's SEC Form S-1 property table lists only one Virginia "IAD4_A" line item for the entire leased IAD4 campus, 58,939 square feet sellable, 77.8 percent leased as of March 31, 2026, rather than separately disclosing an "IAD4-B" line item; this building's existence and address are nonetheless confirmed independently by Csquare's own spec-sheet documentation and this record's own OSM sourcing. Csquare (formerly branded Centersquare, launched April 2024 by Brookfield Infrastructure to combine Cyxtera, acquired out of Chapter 11 bankruptcy for $775 million in a deal completed January 2024, and Evoque, AT&T's divested data center business under Brookfield since 2019) went public via IPO on NASDAQ in July 2026 at $21.00 per share. Csquare's public spec sheet states a campus-wide 57,927 square feet of raised floor, 35.8 megawatts of utility power, 16.8 megawatts of UPS capacity, and 20 megawatts of generator capacity, with standard cage density up to 300 watts per square foot, and SOC 1/2 Type II, PCI-DSS, NIST 800-53 PE High, and ISO 27001 certifications. Csquare does not name a power utility or year-opened date; Dominion Energy serves Loudoun County's Ashburn corridor as a matter of public record.

Ashburn's Data Center Alley is the largest concentration of data center capacity in the world, and Csquare's IAD4 campus sits among dozens of competing hyperscale and colocation operators within a few miles. Csquare's SEC S-1 discloses 389 megawatts of total sellable power capacity across its full 64-facility, 21-market portfolio as of March 31, 2026, and separately discloses that the company's legal predecessor entity, BIF III US Aggregator (Delaware) LLC, was formed in May 2018 as a Brookfield Infrastructure Fund III vehicle, well before the 2024 Cyxtera and Evoque combination that produced the assets tracked across this dataset.

sources.title: Csquare, Inc. Form S-1 Registration Statement (IAD4 reported as single asset "IAD4_A")

profile.research_note: Csquare's SEC S-1 property table reports only one "IAD4_A" line item for the whole IAD4 campus despite two published street addresses; this building's individual square footage is therefore not independently disclosed the way IAD4-A's SEC figure technically is (that figure is itself the whole-campus figure applied to one address).

reading.body:
Centersquare's IAD4-B sits at one of two addresses within the IAD4 campus in Ashburn, Virginia, in the world's largest data center concentration. The campus publishes 35.8 megawatts of utility power and 16.8 megawatts of UPS capacity across 57,927 square feet of raised floor for both IAD4-A and IAD4-B combined; the individual square footage and power allocation between the two buildings are not published separately. At a standard colocation density of 300 watts per square foot, the campus could support roughly 17,400 kilowatts of IT load, or at 40 kilowatts per rack, approximately 435 racks, though this assumes the full published floor space and power are allocated to compute rather than network, power distribution, or other infrastructure.

The campus holds SOC 1/2 Type II, PCI-DSS, NIST 800-53 PE High, and ISO 27001 certifications, qualifying it for secure financial and government workloads. Centersquare reports 389 megawatts of total sellable capacity across 64 facilities in 21 markets as of March 2026, making this one campus a small fraction of the company's portfolio. Dominion Energy supplies power to the Ashburn corridor as the regional utility.

IAD4-B ranks 24th by published megawatts in Virginia, outside the state's top 23 facilities by disclosed capacity. Virginia's 326 mapped data center sites hold 1,375 megawatts of published utility power across only 23 operators willing to disclose figures, meaning most facilities in the state publish nothing. The campus exists in a market where published capacity is rare and majority-held by much larger peers.
